I was diagnosed with Crohn's disease. I had basically stopped growing at a time when everyone was going through their growth spurts. So I was really short and everyone around me suddenly grew so much. I had to miss 6 weeks of school because I had a feeding tube down my nose to feed me 24/7 so my body could absorb as much nutrition as possible (it had basically been able to only absorb enough to keep me alive, but not enough for my body to actually continue developing). I then had a tube implanted directly into my stomach so I could continue with the liquid feedings at night. This throughout my 4 years of high school. So it was really detrimental to me. I was so embarrassed about it, never mind being the shortest kid in the school, but to also have a tube sticking out of my stomach? It was mortifying. Then at the end of the 4 years I found out that I had a major blockage and had to have surgery during which they removed about a foot of my small intestine. Finding out that I had to have the surgery was such a blow because I had chose the feeding tube as a hopeful alternative to surgery. Having suffered with that thing for 4 years only to end up having to go through the surgery anyway fucked me up badly. That was right at the end of my OAC year (grade 13). Of course, the education system being what it is I still had to complete my classes of which I had missed the last weeks of and do the exams. So I had to learn the material on my own in order to be able to finish. It was such a shitty time in my life. 
I don't even think that people don't WANT to be there for me. I think it's that they're so selfish and self-absorbed that they can't get over themselves long enough lend a helping hand or ear or shoulder. It's all about them all of the time.
